exposure: Socioeconomic status (living in lower socioeconomic areas)
outcome: Changes between exclusive breastfeeding and formula-only feeding across subsequent births
cohort: The study included 317,027 mothers in New South Wales, Australia, who had a term singleton live-birth between 2007-2011 and subsequently had another birth.
finding: Infant feeding practices were strongly recurrent (71% for formula-only, 92% for exclusive breastfeeding), with young maternal age, being Australian born or single, smoking during pregnancy, and lower socioeconomic status most strongly associated with repeat formula-only feeding or changing from exclusive breastfeeding to formula-only feeding.
